newsitem.title: USA: Forest Oil begins High Island production.
newsitem.headline: Forest Oil begins High Island production.

text.p: Forest Oil Corp said Thursday production began at year-end from its High Island Block A-549 discovery well in the Gulf of Mexico, offshore Texas.

The well, which was drilled in March 1996, is now producing at the rate of about 17 million cubic feet of natural gas per day with output from the deeper of the two producing zones currently being restricted to diminish the potential for water replacing gas flows from that formation.
The well is owned 50 percent each by Forest and Samedan Oil Corp, the operator, a subsidiary of Noble Affiliates Inc.
Forest Oil said the well originally logged about 200 net feet of true vertical pay in multiple zones.
The well is a dual completion with production flowing from perforations between 10,888 feet and 10,906 feet and between 4,396 feet and 4,772 feet.
Production may be increased from the lower zone upon further evaluation, Forest Oil said. Additional exploratory opportunities on the block are being evaluated by the partners.
High Island A-549 is the second of six previously announced offshore discoveries to be brought on production by Forest Oil, the company noted.

It said completion and development operations at High Island A-274 and West Cameron 615 will be conducted over the next three months, and it is expected both will be on production by the end of the first quarter.
The West Cameron 225 discovery is scheduled for completion in the third quarter, but development plans for the West Cameron 616 discovery have not been finalized.
